guard_streams.source: Building Digital UK Annual Report and Accounts 2024 to 2025
guard_streams.write_limit: Corporate programme accounts and delivery summaries are aggregate operational evidence and do not establish current broadband orderability or measured speed at a selected parcel.

facts.detail: The report records 1,227,000 cumulative premises passed by BDUK interventions.
It records 152,700 premises passed in 2024/25.
England recorded 101,800 premises passed in 2024/25.
Scotland recorded 34,700 premises passed in 2024/25.
Wales recorded 10,700 premises passed in 2024/25.
Northern Ireland recorded 5,500 premises passed in 2024/25.
47,400 delivered premises previously had speeds below 30 Mbit/s.
BDUK published final Superfast and early GIS evaluation reports during the year.
The report states over 95% of UK landmass had 4G coverage from at least one operator.
By 31 March 2025, 45 Extended Area Service sites were live.

guard_streams.source: Local Full Fibre Networks Programme wave one final evaluation
guard_streams.write_limit: Evaluation design, project findings and counterfactual analysis do not prove current broadband availability, orderability or measured speed for a selected parcel.

facts.detail: BDUK published the final evaluation on 14 December 2023.
Ipsos UK conducted the evaluation.
BDUK commissioned Ipsos UK in May 2018.
The evaluation covers four wave-one pilot projects.
West Sussex is one of the evaluated projects.
Tameside is one of the evaluated projects.
The Trans Pennine Initiative is one of the evaluated projects.
The Schools project is one of the evaluated projects.
A synthesis report provides an overview across the projects.
A technical annex details the analytical approach.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Vouchers Evaluation: Impacts and Value for Money Assessment
guard_streams.write_limit: Voucher programme evaluation and counterfactual impact estimates are research evidence and cannot establish current selected-parcel serviceability or measured speed.

facts.detail: BDUK published the evaluation on 20 September 2023.
It is the second analytical report on voucher impacts.
The evaluated product includes GBVS and the Rural Gigabit Connectivity programme.
It examines vouchers issued and connected by March 2021.
It updates counterfactual analysis of technology availability and download speeds.
It analyses firm-level and area-level economic performance.
It includes a 2022 residential beneficiary survey.
It assesses household wellbeing benefits.
It assesses travel and energy-related environmental impacts.
It includes an initial cost-benefit and value-for-money analysis.

facts.detail: BDUK published the research portal on 16 October 2020.
The portal was last updated on 26 June 2026.
It collects work from BDUK Evaluation and Analysis teams.
It has evaluations, in-house research, evaluation plans and commissioned research sections.
The research supports programme design and development.
The team includes analysts, modellers, researchers, economists and designers.
The portal research assesses intervention efficacy.
It supports understanding of impacts from BDUK programmes.
The portal lists the 2026 GigaHubs process review.
It lists plans for Project Gigabit, Hubs, LFFN and Shared Rural Network evaluations.

guard_streams.source: GigaHubs Process Review Theory of Change
guard_streams.write_limit: A programme theory of change describes intended mechanisms, outputs and outcomes; it does not prove current selected-parcel orderability or measured broadband speed.

facts.detail: BDUK published the GigaHubs Theory of Change on 26 June 2026.
Belmana authored the report and the study involved Belmana and GC Insight.
GigaHubs formed part of Project Gigabit.
The programme focused on schools, GP surgeries, libraries and other public buildings.
The programme targeted rural and remote areas.
The review records that over 3,000 schools were contacted manually during scoping.
Benefits-monitoring information was typically expected quarterly for three years after build completion.
A key output was gigabit-capable broadband to sites outside commercial plans.
A key output was making infrastructure available in previously unviable areas.
Long-term site benefits depend on activation and take-up of the available service.
